question: Do you offer free on-site trim estimates?
answer: Yes. We visit, inspect fascia, soffits, corners and windows, and give you an itemized scope and estimate.

question: Do you do repairs, or only full replacement?
answer: Both. We repair what's still sound and replace when that's the safer long-term fix. Either way, we'll explain why.

question: What trim materials do you use?
answer: Common exterior materials used on the Cape, including wood and PVC. We recommend based on exposure, budget and look.

question: Do you repair fascia and soffits too?
answer: Yes. They're some of the most common failure points in coastal weather.

question: How long does a trim project take?
answer: It depends on how many areas need work and whether there's hidden rot. You'll get a timeline after the visit.

question: What types of siding do you work with?
answer: Cedar shingle, vinyl and fiber cement, plus the trim, fascia and soffits around them.

question: Can you match my existing siding?
answer: When possible. If it's discontinued or has aged, we'll show you the closest option.

question: Can you repair one section instead of replacing everything?
answer: Often, yes. Many homes need a targeted repair. We'll explain when replacement is the better long-term choice.

question: What if there's hidden rot behind the siding?
answer: We document it and repair the compromised backing or sheathing before closing up.

question: How long do siding repairs take?
answer: It depends on scope and weather. You'll get a timeline after the evaluation, before work starts.

question: Do you build new decks or only repair?
answer: Both. We do new builds, full rebuilds, repairs and upgrades.

question: Can you replace boards without rebuilding the frame?
answer: Sometimes. If the framing is solid, we can replace boards only. We'll check and tell you honestly.

question: Wood or composite?
answer: We build with both and will walk you through the trade-offs in look, maintenance and budget.

question: How do you prevent wobble, bounce and squeaks?
answer: Careful layout, accurate framing and proper fastening.

question: Do you build stairs and railings?
answer: Yes, new and replacement stairs and railings, built safe and straight.

question: Do you repair windows and doors or only replace them?
answer: Both, whichever makes the most sense for each unit.

question: Can you replace a single window or door?
answer: Yes, and we can match the existing style and size.

question: What types do you install?
answer: Double-hung, casement, sliders, picture windows, entry doors and sliding patio doors.

question: I have drafts or water around a window. Can you fix it?
answer: Yes. We install every opening as a system: flashing, sealing, insulation and clean trim transitions.

question: Do you repair the trim around windows?
answer: Yes, trim repair and finishing are part of what we do.

question: Should I repair or replace my roof?
answer: Many leaks come from flashing, valleys, edges or a small damaged area. We'll tell you honestly whether a targeted repair makes sense.

question: What are the most common roof repairs on Cape Cod?
answer: Storm damage, missing or lifted shingles, chimney and skylight flashing, valley leaks, nail pops, vent boots and edge problems.

question: How fast can you respond to an active leak?
answer: We prioritize active leaks when we can. Timing depends on weather and schedule, and we'll set the soonest available visit.

question: Will the repair match my existing shingles?
answer: When possible. Otherwise we'll show you the closest option.

question: Can you help with an insurance claim?
answer: We provide photos and documentation. You work with your insurer on approvals and coverage.

question: Do I need a special permit to build an ADU in Massachusetts?
answer: In most single-family zoning districts, no. ADUs up to 900 sq ft are allowed by right. You'll still need a building permit, and your town may have local rules on things like setbacks and parking.

question: How big can my ADU be?
answer: Up to 900 sq ft or half the size of your main home, whichever is smaller.

question: Can I rent out my ADU?
answer: In general, yes. State law doesn't require the owner to live on the property. Some towns limit short-term rentals, so check your town's rules.

question: What about septic on Cape Cod?
answer: Adding a bedroom may require a septic review or upgrade. We'll talk through this early, so there are no surprises.

question: How long does an ADU project take?
answer: It depends on the type of ADU and the permit timeline in your town. You'll get a clear schedule with your estimate.

question: Do you offer free estimates?
answer: Yes. We provide free on-site estimates, and every quote is itemized so you can see exactly what's included.

question: Which towns do you serve?
answer: We're based in Sandwich, MA and work across Cape Cod, from the Upper Cape to Provincetown, plus Plymouth. See our [service areas](/service-areas/), or tell us your town or ZIP and we'll confirm.

question: Are you licensed and insured?
answer: Yes. We're licensed (HIC/CSL) and insured in Massachusetts, and BBB accredited. A certificate of insurance is available on request.

question: Do you repair, or only replace?
answer: Both. If a repair will hold up, we'll recommend it. If replacement is the safer long-term fix, we'll explain why.

question: How long will my project take?
answer: It depends on scope. After the site visit you'll get a realistic timeline in writing.

question: Do you offer financing?
answer: Yes. Ask about it with your estimate, or see our [financing page](/financing-options/).

question: Do you offer a warranty?
answer: Yes, a workmanship warranty. Terms depend on scope and materials and are explained in writing.

question: Will checking my options affect my credit score?
answer: No. You can check your options without affecting your credit score.

question: How fast is approval?
answer: Approval is fast, and funds can be available in as little as 24 hours.

question: Can I pay it off early?
answer: Yes. There are no prepayment penalties.

question: How do I get started?
answer: Request a free estimate and mention you're interested in financing. We'll walk you through the next steps.

question: Where is Castro Finish Carpentry located?
answer: Our shop is in Sandwich, MA. We serve all of Sandwich, including the village, East Sandwich, Forestdale and South Sandwich, and the rest of Cape Cod.

question: Do you take small repair jobs in Sandwich?
answer: Yes. A rotted sill, a sticking door or a few courses of shingle are all worth a call. Being local makes small jobs practical.

question: Do you work on antique homes in Sandwich Village?
answer: Yes. On older homes we repair and match original trim where it's sound, and replace only what has failed.

question: Does my project need historic district approval?
answer: If the home is in the Old King's Highway district and the change is visible from a public way, it usually does. We'll tell you at the estimate and plan around the review.

question: Do you work in Dennis Port and West Dennis?
answer: Yes, all of Dennis: Dennis Village, East Dennis, South Dennis, West Dennis and Dennis Port.

question: Can you repair a rental property's deck before the summer season?
answer: Yes. Tell us your booking dates when you request the estimate, and we'll plan the work around them.

question: Do you build new decks in Dennis or only repair them?
answer: Both. New decks, full rebuilds, board replacement, railings and stairs, in wood or composite.

question: My home is on Route 6A. Is that a problem?
answer: Not a problem, just a step. Visible exterior changes in the Old King's Highway district may need committee approval, and we'll plan the timeline around it.

question: Do you work in East Orleans and South Orleans?
answer: Yes, all of Orleans, including the village, East Orleans and South Orleans.

question: What trim holds up best near Nauset or Pleasant Bay?
answer: On exposed walls we often recommend PVC or cellular trim with stainless or coated fasteners. Wood still works where it's protected. We'll go through options at the estimate.

question: I don't live in Orleans year-round. Can you still do the work?
answer: Yes. We agree the scope and price in writing and keep you updated with photos, so you don't need to be on site.

question: Do you replace cedar shingles or only repair them?
answer: Both. Sometimes a few courses are enough. When the wall has reached its limit, we re-shingle with proper flashing at every window and corner.

question: Do you work in North Chatham, South Chatham and Chathamport?
answer: Yes, all of Chatham, including North, South and West Chatham and Chathamport.

question: I'm not in Chatham full-time. Can you manage the job while I'm away?
answer: Yes. We agree the scope in writing, send photos when we find something hidden, and keep you updated through the job.

question: Can you match existing trim profiles and details?
answer: Usually, yes. Finish detail is our specialty. If a profile is no longer made, we'll show you the closest match before installing.

question: Wood or composite for a Chatham deck?
answer: Both work. Composite needs less upkeep in salt air; wood can suit a traditional home. We'll compare look, maintenance and budget.

question: Do you really come out to Provincetown and Truro?
answer: Yes. We've worked in Provincetown, and we serve the whole Outer Cape, including Truro and North Truro.

question: Will my project need historic district approval?
answer: In much of Provincetown, visible exterior changes go through the historic district commission. We'll tell you what's likely needed before you commit.

question: How do you handle tight lots and parking in Provincetown?
answer: We plan deliveries, staging and parking with you before the job starts, so the street and your neighbors aren't an afterthought.

question: Can you work on my rental between bookings?
answer: Yes. Share your booking calendar with the estimate request and we'll plan around it, ideally in the off-season.

question: Have you worked in Plymouth before?
answer: Yes. Recent work includes new siding, roofing and window trim on a church in Plymouth, shown above.

question: Do you work in Plymouth even though it's off-Cape?
answer: Yes. Plymouth is part of our regular service area, a short drive over the Sagamore Bridge from our Sandwich shop.

question: Do you work in the Pinehills and Manomet?
answer: Yes, all of Plymouth, including downtown, North Plymouth, Manomet, Cedarville, White Horse Beach and the Pinehills.

question: Can you replace my deck boards with composite?
answer: Often, yes, if the framing is solid. We check the structure first and tell you honestly whether boards alone make sense.

question: Do you fix PVC trim that has separated?
answer: Yes. Open joints in PVC trim usually come from expansion and fastening; we re-fasten, re-join and seal them properly.
